title: Dover vs Greenhouse: Which Is Better? (August 2026)
summary: Dover vs Greenhouse for Aug. 2026: pricing, features, setup time, and AI. Dover offers a free ATS while Greenhouse costs $10K-$75K+ annually.
body_markdown:
When comparing Greenhouse with Dover, the real question becomes whether your team needs the enterprise-level depth and configurability of a heavyweight ATS or the simplified, startup-friendly simplicity of a modern recruiting system. Both tools help you hire, but they differ dramatically in learning curve, pricing, implementation timelines, and how much ongoing maintenance they demand from your team. Below, we break down the necessary differences (features, costs, setup, and everyday usability) between[Dover vs Greenhouse](https://www.dover.com/) so you can clearly understand which system aligns best with your hiring needs and growth stage.


**TLDR:**


-


Dover offers a free ATS with unlimited jobs and users, plus a premium tier at $199/mo, while Greenhouse’s pricing is quote-based.


-


You can start hiring on Dover immediately with no setup, versus days to weeks of configuration for Greenhouse.


-


Dover’s recruiter marketplace charges by the hour (low thousands per hire) versus 20 to 25% of salary at agencies.


-


Dover combines a free ATS with access to vetted recruiters who work as an extension of your team.


-


Dover centralizes sourcing, outreach, and ATS workflows in one place, while Greenhouse provides a core feature set, with some specialized capabilities requiring additional modules or third-party tools.


## What Is Greenhouse?


Greenhouse is an[applicant tracking system](https://sg.indeed.com/career-advice/career-development/what-are-applicant-tracking-systems) built for mid-market and enterprise companies that need structured hiring workflows. The product includes interview scheduling, candidate tracking, customizable hiring stages, and scorecard-based evaluations. Greenhouse also offers third-party integrations and AI features like interview preparation and candidate summaries for organizations managing high-volume hiring across multiple departments.


## What Is Dover?


Dover is a recruiting solution that pairs a[free ATS](https://www.dover.com/ats) with a marketplace of vetted recruiters. The company targets early-stage and growing startups that need both software and recruiting help without the overhead of full-time hires or agency retainers.


The free ATS includes unlimited jobs and users, candidate tracking, automated interview scheduling, one-click posting to 100+ job boards, Google and Microsoft email integration, email templates and interview scorecards, a careers page builder, and a[Chrome sourcing extension](https://help.dover.com/en/articles/6301760-dover-sourcing-extension) . AI-powered resume screening and the AI interview notetaker are available on the premium tier at $199/mo.


The recruiting marketplace lets companies hire experienced recruiters by the hour. Each company gets one dedicated recruiter who handles sourcing, outreach, and pipeline building. This differs from traditional agency models where jobs get distributed to multiple recruiters at once.


## Implementation and Setup Complexity


Greenhouse offers 500+ integrations and configurable workflows for HR teams building out recruiting tech stacks. This comes with a[learning curve](https://www.dover.com/blog/enterprise-ats-problems-for-startups) . Users report needing dedicated HR tech resources to configure interview kits, scorecards, approval chains, and workflows. Implementation can take days to several weeks depending on team size and complexity.


Dover’s ATS is ready to use immediately. You can create a job, post it to 100+ boards, and start receiving candidates on day one. No configuration needed, no training required. The interface is built for founders and small teams who need to hire now.


### Setup Timeline Comparison


With Greenhouse, expect onboarding calls, admin training sessions, and workflow mapping before your team feels ready to use the system. Dover’s core features work out of the box.


The right fit depends on your timeline. Greenhouse works for teams with time to invest in setup and ongoing administration. Dover works for teams that need to start hiring immediately.


## Features and Functionality


Greenhouse offers structured hiring capabilities including customizable interview kits, scorecard evaluations, reporting dashboards, and[candidate relationship management tools](https://indeedflex.com/blog/for-employers/candidate-relationship-management-systems-what-you-need-to-know/) . These work well for companies with experienced recruiting teams needing detailed control over each hiring stage.


Many of these features are tier-locked. Advanced automation, enhanced reporting, and certain integrations require upgrading to higher-priced plans, so the entry-level subscription may lack the functionality you need.


Dover’s free ATS includes unlimited jobs and users, one-click posting to 100+ job boards, automated scheduling and communications, Google and Microsoft email integration, email templates and interview scorecards, a Chrome sourcing extension, and a careers page builder. AI-powered resume screening (up to 2,000 candidate scores per month) and the AI interview notetaker are available on the premium tier at $199/mo.


### When to Layer a Recruiter on Top of Your ATS


For most inbound hiring and standard roles, an ATS handles the workflow: posting jobs, tracking candidates, scheduling interviews, and moving applicants through stages. The calculus shifts when roles get harder to fill, such as a senior technical hire, a function with a shallow candidate pool, or a stretch of high-volume hiring with no dedicated recruiting bandwidth. In those situations, software alone rarely closes the gap.


Dover includes access to a[recruiter marketplace](https://www.dover.com/blog/ats-with-fractional-recruiter-guide) built for exactly that inflection point. Each recruiter in the marketplace carries verified reviews from prior client engagements, so you can assess fit before committing. This is the same infrastructure that fractional recruiting agencies rely on to run end-to-end searches: one dedicated recruiter integrates with your team, handling sourcing, outreach, and pipeline building without the overhead of a full-time hire or agency retainer. Both the recruiter and your internal team work inside the same ATS, giving everyone real-time visibility into sourcing activity and candidate flow with no coordination overhead or duplicate outreach.


Greenhouse focuses on process depth for teams with dedicated recruiting headcount. Dover pairs its workflow tools with on-demand human recruiting capacity for teams that need both the software and the people.


## AI and Automation Capabilities


Greenhouse has expanded its AI capabilities considerably through 2025 and into 2026. The platform now includes Greenhouse Notetaker, which records and transcribes interviews and maps notes to scorecard questions; Voice AI, which delivers structured voice screening conversations scored against your team’s criteria; an Analytics Chart Agent that converts plain-text questions into charts without manual setup (launched June 2026); and a Candidate Insights Agent that surfaces candidate summaries from scorecards, notes, and activity (expected Q3 2026). These features support recruiters by reducing manual work and sharpening hiring signal. Greenhouse frames its AI as augmenting human decision-making, which fits teams with trained recruiters who want data to inform their process.


These AI capabilities are newer additions and may require higher-tier subscriptions. Teams on entry-level plans might not have full access without upgrading.


Dover builds automation into the core product. The free tier covers automated scheduling and communications, email templates, interview scorecards, and Google and Microsoft email integration. The premium tier at $199/mo adds[AI-powered resume screening](https://www.dover.com/blog/ai-recruiting-software-ats) that scores and ranks every applicant based on job requirements (up to 2,000 scores per month, no API key required), plus an AI interview notetaker that joins video calls, transcribes conversations, and fills out feedback forms so interviewers can focus on the conversation.


Greenhouse layers AI onto workflows designed for recruiting professionals who manage structured processes. Dover’s automation lets founders and lean teams execute recruiting without dedicated HR headcount.


## Integrations and Ecosystem


Greenhouse offers an integration marketplace with over 500 pre-built connections, including[HRIS systems](https://www.business.com/hr-software/hris/) , background check providers, assessment tools, and video interviewing solutions. This breadth serves enterprises building complex recruiting tech stacks with specialized tools for each hiring function.


Many integrations require additional subscriptions from third-party vendors, adding costs beyond Greenhouse’s base pricing. Some integration capabilities are restricted to higher subscription tiers.


Dover includes core integrations in the free ATS. Calendar syncing works with Google Calendar and Outlook for automated scheduling. Job board distribution covers 70+ boards without separate accounts.


The agency management portal centralizes candidate submissions and status tracking when working with external recruiters. Dover’s Chrome sourcing extension pulls candidate contact information directly from LinkedIn for immediate outreach.


### Integration Philosophy


Greenhouse optimizes for maximum flexibility across hundreds of tools. Dover focuses on the integrations early-stage teams use daily. The difference is breadth for complex requirements versus necessary connectivity that works out of the box.

## Why Dover Is the Better Choice


Greenhouse works for mid-market and enterprise companies with dedicated HR teams, substantial recruiting budgets (contracts typically run $10,000 to $75,000+ per year based on[Vendr July 2026 buyer data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/greenhouse) ), and time for implementation. Organizations with these resources can take advantage of the depth and customization Greenhouse offers.


For startups, Dover removes the cost barrier with a free ATS that includes automated scheduling, multi-board posting, email templates, and interview scorecards. Teams that want AI-powered resume screening and the AI interview notetaker can upgrade to the premium tier at $199/mo. You can start hiring immediately without setup complexity or training.


Dover’s model gives companies access to experienced fractional recruiters through the same infrastructure that fractional recruiting agencies are built on. Each recruiter in the marketplace has verified client reviews, so the selection process is transparent instead of opaque. You pay hourly only when hiring, with most companies averaging $2,000 to $7,000 per hire (rates vary by role and recruiter) compared to the $25,000+ fees traditional agencies typically charge.


## FAQs


### How quickly can I start hiring with each tool?


Dover’s ATS works immediately; you can create a job, post to 100+ boards, and receive candidates on day one without configuration or training. Greenhouse requires onboarding calls, admin training, and workflow mapping that typically takes weeks before your team is ready to use the system effectively.


### Do I need a recruiter if I’m already using an ATS?


An ATS handles the mechanics of hiring: posting jobs, tracking applicants, scheduling, and moving candidates through stages. For roles with strong inbound applicant flow, that coverage is often enough. A recruiter adds value when the ATS alone can’t fill the top of the funnel. This tends to happen for senior or specialized roles where the right candidates aren’t actively applying, when hiring velocity outpaces what a small team can manage, or when sourcing passive candidates requires dedicated outreach effort. The two work together rather than as substitutes: the ATS gives both your internal team and any recruiter a shared view of the pipeline, while the recruiter drives active sourcing the software can’t replicate on its own.


### What AI features does Dover include?


Dover’s free ATS includes automated scheduling and communications, email templates, and interview scorecards. AI-powered resume screening (up to 2,000 candidate scores per month) and the AI interview notetaker are available on the premium tier at $199/mo. The premium tier does not require an API key, though users can connect their own for unlimited scoring.


## Final Thoughts on Selecting Your Recruiting Software


Choosing between[Dover vs Greenhouse](https://www.dover.com/) comes down to your team’s stage, hiring velocity, and functional needs. Startups and lean teams often benefit most from Dover’s free ATS, simplified workflows, and flexible recruiter marketplace, while mid-market and enterprise organizations tend to get more value from Greenhouse’s extensive customization and structured processes. Neither tool is universally better. They’re built for different growth phases and resourcing levels, so focus on the solution that removes your hiring bottlenecks today and can scale with where your company is heading next. Dover is one place to start if you want both ends covered: a free ATS that manages your pipeline paired with on-demand fractional recruiters when searches need more hands-on support, averaging $2,000 to $7,000 per hire on average with no retainer required.
